meaning.evidence: Every beat survives: the house-party, "Liberty Hall", eight and eight-twenty, the creak, Lorna Doone, the 1902 mandolin photo, the barges, the sonnets, the Alps inscription kept verbatim, Emerson, "Ten past nine, that's all!", skipping the bath.

sense.evidence: Mostly exact ("have a squiz at the pictures", "dodgy-looking barges", "Bit of a scruffy-looking lot"), but "open it, ever so politely" shifts "modestly" (discreetly) toward courtesy, and "Not bad, I s'pose" brings in a first-person narrator the second-person piece lacks.

authenticity.evidence: Natural: "Sleep in as long as you like", "kill a bit of time", "Oh, righto then!". "Some people _are_ like that. Too right they are." is a bolted-on tag.

register.evidence: Light level-2 touches ("brekkie", "beaut", "squiz", "dodgy") on a plain modern retelling; no swearing.

tone.evidence: The mock-solemn comedy of the anxious guest is intact: "Never touch a sonnet before breakfast", "We'll read it just to spite 'em."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly; the added "Too right they are." after the italic punchline flattens it.

variety.evidence: Varied light slang with nothing leaned on: "brekkie", "beaut", "squiz", "dodgy", "righto", "on the sly", "a wander round".

problems.quote: Some people _are_ like that. Too right they are.

tone.evidence: The dry, self-mocking comedy comes through whole: "Never touch a sonnet before breakfast", "We'll read it just out of spite."

variety.evidence: Modest but varied set; nothing repeated.
